- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

1	/-

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyH1Locus
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LocalGenerators
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.H1BaseFieldInvariance
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiCurve
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# DAT-C C2 — the rank-1 H⁰ export and the generator kit
    13	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-3 Σ-RANK1, §2 (N1)/(N3))
    14	
    15	On the fibrewise h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization
    16	`χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`, the datum engine's `H⁰` is an **invertible** module: finite,
    17	projective, and of stalk-rank exactly `1`.  This is the rank export the engine
    18	(`datumRigidEngine`, `Cohomology/GluedSheafEngine.lean`) leaves open — it delivers
    19	finite + projective, never `rankAtStalk = 1`.
    20	
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_relCurve` — the χ transport `χ(𝒪_{C_L}) = 1 − n` to every
    22	  field `L` of the test tower (base-field invariance of the genus, `chi_moduleKSheaf`
    23	  + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the private lemma of `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`).
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one` — **the fibre
    25	  computation**: for a datum whose fibre class over `L` has `classDeg = n`, with `H¹` of
    26	  the base-changed sheaf vanishing, `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1` — the Riemann–Roch anchor
    27	  `h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` (`n + (1 − n)`) read through the presentation
    28	  bridge `presentationSheafIso`.  The fibre geometric package is threaded as instance
    29	  arguments (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one` — **Σ-RANK1,
    31	  the datum-level export**: on the vanishing locus (fibre degree `n`, `χ = 1 − n`),
    32	  `Module.rankAtStalk (H⁰(F_D)) p = 1`.  Route: `Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as
    33	  the `κ(p)`-fibre dimension; `datumH0BaseChange` (on the nose) identifies the fibre with
    34	  `H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`; the fibre computation above pins it at `1`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one` — the
    36	  certified-family specialization (**N1**): for `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus
    37	  `V`, the divisor datum `D_G := G.adaptation.divisorDatum` has invertible `H⁰`.  The
    38	  fibre-degree hypothesis is discharged uniformly by `DivFamZar.classDeg_picClass` (the
    39	  fibre class has `classDeg = n` at every field).
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily.exists_fibrewise_generator_divisorDatum`
    41	  — **N3, the generator kit**: since `H⁰(F_{D_G})` is projective of rank `1` (hence has a
    42	  nontrivial fibre at every prime of the locus), a fibrewise-nonzero **global** section
    43	  exists Zariski-locally (`Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`).
    44	
    45	Noetherian discipline (worksheet §2): every rank statement carries `[IsNoetherianRing S]`
    46	through the engine; the arbitrary-test consumers reach it through RE-5 stages.
    47	-/
    48	
    49	set_option autoImplicit false
    50	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    51	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    52	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
    53	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    58	open scoped TensorProduct
    59	
    60	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    61	
    62	open AlgebraicJacobian Scheme
    63	
    64	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    65	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    66	
    67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    68	variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    69	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {n : ℕ}
    70	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    71	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    72	
    73	/-- The standing `C.left`-over-`k` structure, keyed on `C.hom` — the instance the base
    74	χ-normalization `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is phrased against (defeq to `.ofHom C.hom`, so
    75	`chi_moduleKSheaf C` unifies with it). -/
    76	noncomputable local instance instOverCleftRankOne : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
    77	
    78	/-! ## The χ transport to the fibre curve -/
    79	
    80	/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` at every field extension**, from the base normalization
    81	(`chi_moduleKSheaf` at the base-changed bundle + `genus_baseField`; a re-derivation of the
    82	`DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel` private lemma). -/
    83	theorem chi_relCurve (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    84	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    85	    Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) := by
    86	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle C L).hom := instIsProperSndLeft C L
    87	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    88	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C L
    89	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    90	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C L
    91	  have h1 : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L)
    92	      = 1 - (genus (baseChangeBundle C L) : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle C L)
    93	  have h2 : genus (baseChangeBundle C L) = genus C := genus_baseField C L
    94	  have h3 : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := chi_moduleKSheaf C
    95	  have h4 : (genus C : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) := by rw [h3] at hχ; linarith
    96	  rw [h1, h2, h4]
    97	
    98	/-! ## The fibre computation: `h⁰(C_L, F_{D_L}) = 1`
    99	
   100	The fibre geometric instances (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`) are threaded as instance
   101	arguments — they cannot be synthesized through the `relCurve` `def` barrier, so consumers
   102	install them by `haveI` (the `degAt_abelDiv` block, I-0249 (iv)) before calling. -/
   103	
   104	/-- **The fibre h⁰ pin**: for a datum whose fibre class over the field `L` has
   105	`classDeg = n`, with the base χ-normalization and vanishing `H¹` of the base-changed
   106	sheaf, the fibre global-section count is exactly `1` — the Riemann–Roch rank anchor
   107	`h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi` read through the presentation bridge
   108	`presentationSheafIso`, at `n + (1 − n)`. -/
   109	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one
   110	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π)
   111	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   112	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra S L] [IsScalarTower k S L]
   113	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   114	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   115	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   116	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   117	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   118	    (hg : classDeg L (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ))
   119	    (hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange L).sheaf 1)) :
   120	    Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = 1 := by
   121	  set P : (relCurve C L).MeromorphicPresentation :=
   122	    Scheme.MeromorphicPresentation.ofCocycle (D.baseChange L).pointedCover
   123	      (gluedSubordCocycle (D.baseChange L).isGluingCocycle
   124	        (D.baseChange L).pointedCover (D.baseChange L).pieceIndex
   125	        fun _ => le_rfl) with hP
   126	  have hsubP : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (P.gluedSheaf L) 1) :=
   127	    (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L)) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp
   128	      hsub
   129	  have h0eq : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf = Sheaf.h0 (P.gluedSheaf L) :=
   130	    Sheaf.h0_congr (presentationSheafIso (D.baseChange L))
   131	  have hformula := h0_gluedSheaf_eq_classDeg_add_chi L P hsubP
   132	  have hPclass : P.picClass = (D.baseChange L).cechPicClass := rfl
   133	  have hint : (Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange L).sheaf : ℤ) = 1 := by
   134	    rw [h0eq, hformula, hPclass, hg, chi_relCurve hχ L]; ring
   135	  exact_mod_cast hint
   136	
   137	/-! ## Σ-RANK1: the rank-1 export on the vanishing locus -/
   138	
   139	/-- **Σ-RANK1, the datum-level rank export** (worksheet GAP-3): on the fibrewise
   140	h¹-vanishing locus, at fibre degree `n` with the base χ-normalization `χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n`,
   141	the datum engine's `H⁰` has stalk-rank exactly `1` at `p`.
   142	
   143	`Module.rankAtStalk_eq` reads the rank as the `κ(p)`-dimension of the fibre
   144	`κ(p) ⊗[S] H⁰`; the on-the-nose base change `datumH0BaseChange` identifies this fibre with
   145	`H⁰(C_{κ(p)}, F_{D_{κ(p)}})`, whose dimension is `1` by the fibre computation. The global
   146	fibrewise hypothesis `hfib` supplies finiteness/projectivity (hence flatness) through
   147	`datumRigidEngine`. -/
   148	theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one
   149	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C S π) [IsNoetherianRing S]
   150	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   151	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   152	    (hfib : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S,
   153	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[S] q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   154	    (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   155	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   157	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   158	    [QuasiCompact
   159	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   160	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   161	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   162	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   163	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)]
   164	    (hg : classDeg p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   165	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = (n : ℤ)) :
   166	    Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 := by
   167	  obtain ⟨-, hfin, hproj⟩ := datumRigidEngine D hπ hfib
   168	  haveI := hfin
   169	  haveI := hproj
   170	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 := datum_subsingleton_pairH1 D hπ hfib
   171	  have hfibre : Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf = 1 :=
   172	    D.h0_sheaf_baseChange_eq_one hχ p.asIdeal.ResidueField hg
   173	      (D.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField hH1)
   174	  calc Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p
   175	      = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   176	          (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[S] (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)) :=
   177	        Module.rankAtStalk_eq p
   178	    _ = Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   179	          (Sheaf.HModule (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf 0) :=

   181	    _ = Sheaf.h0 (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).sheaf := rfl
   182	    _ = 1 := hfibre

   187	/-- (Implementation) The fibre class of the divisor datum has `classDeg = n` at `κ(p)`:

   189	private theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.classDeg_baseChange_divisorDatum
   190	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) (p : PrimeSpectrum S)
   191	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   193	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   194	    [QuasiCompact
   195	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField))]
   196	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   197	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   199	      (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1)] :

   210	divisor family `G` landing in the h¹-vanishing locus `V` (`hvan`), the divisor datum

   214	the fibre class of `D_G` at `κ(p)` is the base change of `G.eqns`, which has

   216	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.rankAtStalk_divisorDatum_eq_one
   217	    (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C S π n) [IsNoetherianRing S]

     9	/-!
    10	# Base-change instances for the curve over an extension field (gap G-D5(a))
    11	
    12	For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` (smooth of relative dimension one, proper and
    13	geometrically irreducible over the field `k`) and a field extension `K` of `k`
    14	(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file installs — **as instances that fire by typeclass
    15	resolution** — every hypothesis of the landed degree/Riemann–Roch stack
    16	(`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Degree`) for the base-changed curve
    17	
    18	`C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,
    19	
    20	viewed as a `K`-scheme via the **second projection** `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This is
    21	exactly the `Over`-instance spelling that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver`
    22	uses (`.ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`), but keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`
    23	spelling that the Riemann–Roch files consume, rather than on the `relCurve C K` `def`.
    24	
    25	The single geometric input is the pullback bridge `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`
    26	(`Cohomology.SectionsBaseChange`): the second projection `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left` is the
    27	base change of the structure morphism `C.hom` along `overSpec k K ⟶ Spec k`. Every morphism
    28	property then transports by `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange` (smooth of relative
    29	dimension one, proper, geometrically irreducible), and integrality of `C_K` is
    30	`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced` applied to the base change (geometric
    31	irreducibility is transported; geometric reducedness comes for free from smoothness).
    32	
    33	## Main instances (keyed for the Riemann–Roch stack)
    34	
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instOverBaseChange` — item 1: `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is a `K`-scheme
    36	  via the second projection; `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K = (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`
    37	  definitionally (`baseChange_over_eq_snd_left`).
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft`,
    39	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperSndLeft`,
    40	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft` — the base-change transport of the
    41	  standing bundle onto the raw morphism `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` (item 2),
    43	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperBaseChange`,
    44	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactBaseChange` (item 4) — the same properties in the
    45	  `↘`-spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K` that `classDeg` queries.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsIntegralBaseChange` (item 3): `C_K` is integral.
    47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange`,
    48	  `AlgebraicGeometry.instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange` (item 5): the two structure-sheaf
    49	  cohomology finiteness instances over `K`.
    50	
    51	The acceptance smoke test (item 6) verifies that the landed `classDeg K` typechecks on `C_K`
    52	with every hypothesis inferred by resolution.
    53	-/
    54	
    55	set_option autoImplicit false
    56	
    57	universe u
    58	
    59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    60	
    61	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    62	
    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    64	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    65	  (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    66	
    67	/-! ## Item 1: the `K`-scheme structure via the second projection -/
    68	
    69	/-- **Item 1.** The base-changed curve `C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is a scheme over
    70	`Spec K` via the **second projection** `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This is the same
    71	structure morphism that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver` installs, but keyed on
    72	the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` spelling consumed by the Riemann–Roch/degree stack (rather than
    73	on the `relCurve C K` `def`). -/
    74	noncomputable instance instOverBaseChange :
    75	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left).Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
    76	  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left
    77	
    78	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
    79	/-- The structure morphism installed by `instOverBaseChange` is, definitionally, the second
    80	projection `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This equation is `rfl`; it lets a consumer rewrite
    81	the `↘`-spelling that `classDeg` uses into the raw projection the base-change lemmas produce
    82	(and back), and pins the alignment with `relCurve.instOver`. -/
    83	theorem baseChange_over_eq_snd_left :
    84	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) = (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-! ## Transport of the standing bundle onto the raw second projection
    88	
    89	Every property is transported from `C.hom` along the base-change square
    90	`Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k K)`, whose right leg is the second projection. These are
    91	keyed on the raw morphism `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`, which is what the bundled curve
    92	`Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left` feeds to the landed curve-level instances
    93	(`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced`, `moduleFinite_hModule_zero`/`_one`). -/
    94	
    95	/-- **Base change of smooth-of-relative-dimension-one.** The second projection is smooth of
    96	relative dimension one over `K`, by `smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange`. -/
    97	instance instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft :
    98	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
    99	  haveI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
   100	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
   101	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1)
   102	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k K)) inferInstance
   103	
   104	/-- **Base change of properness.** The second projection is proper over `K`
   105	(`IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`). -/
   106	instance instIsProperSndLeft : IsProper (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
   107	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsProper)
   108	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k K)) inferInstance
   109	
   110	/-- **Base change of geometric irreducibility.** The second projection is geometrically
   111	irreducible over `K` (`GeometricallyIrreducible` is stable under base change). -/
   112	instance instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft :
   113	    GeometricallyIrreducible (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
   114	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @GeometricallyIrreducible)
   115	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k K)) inferInstance
   116	
   117	/-! ## The properties in the `↘`-spelling consumed by `classDeg`
   118	
   119	The degree stack phrases smoothness and quasi-compactness on `X ↘ Spec K`. Since
   120	`(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K` is definitionally `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`
   121	(`baseChange_over_eq_snd_left`), these bridge instances are the transported raw instances,
   122	now discoverable under the `↘`-key. -/
   123	
   124	/-- **Item 2.** `C_K` is smooth of relative dimension one over `K`, in the `↘`-spelling. -/
   125	instance instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange :
   126	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   127	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
   128	
   129	/-- **Item 4a.** `C_K` is proper over `K`, in the `↘`-spelling. -/
   130	instance instIsProperBaseChange :
   131	    IsProper ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   132	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
   133	
   134	/-- **Item 4b.** `C_K` is quasi-compact over `K`, in the `↘`-spelling (properness gives
   135	quasi-compactness through `UniversallyClosed`). -/
   136	instance instQuasiCompactBaseChange :
   137	    QuasiCompact ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
   138	  inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
   139	
   140	/-! ## Item 3: integrality of the base-changed curve
   141	
   142	Geometric irreducibility (transported above) together with geometric reducedness (free from
   143	smoothness, `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`) gives integrality, via the landed
   144	`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced` applied to the bundled base-changed curve. -/
   145	
   146	/-- **Item 3.** The base-changed curve `C_K` is integral: it is geometrically irreducible and
   147	geometrically reduced over `K`. This is the genuine content of gap G-D5(a) — the definition of
   148	geometric irreducibility/reducedness of `C/k` gives integrality of `C ⊗_k K` for *every* field
   149	extension `K`. The bundled curve `Over.mk (snd …)` reroutes the raw-morphism instances above to
   150	the `X.hom` shape that `isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced` reads (geometric reducedness is
   151	free from smoothness). -/
   152	instance instIsIntegralBaseChange : IsIntegral ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left) :=
   153	  let bundled : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left
   154	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible bundled.hom := instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C K
   155	  haveI : GeometricallyReduced bundled.hom :=
   156	    (inferInstance : GeometricallyReduced (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
   157	  isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced bundled
   158	
   159	/-! ## Item 5: structure-sheaf cohomology finiteness over `K`
   160	
   161	The landed curve-level finiteness instances `moduleFinite_hModule_zero`/`_one`, applied to the
   162	bundled base-changed curve `Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left` (whose structure morphism is
   163	the raw second projection carrying the transported standing bundle), keyed for the
   164	`(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K` spelling that `classDeg` queries. -/
   165	
   166	/-- **Item 5a.** `H⁰(C_K, 𝒪)` is a finite `K`-module. -/
   167	instance instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange :
   168	    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 0) :=
   169	  let bundled : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left
   170	  haveI : IsProper bundled.hom := instIsProperSndLeft C K
   171	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 bundled.hom := instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C K
   172	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible bundled.hom := instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C K
   173	  moduleFinite_hModule_zero bundled
   174	
   175	/-- **Item 5b.** `H¹(C_K, 𝒪)` is a finite `K`-module. -/
   176	instance instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange :
   177	    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) 1) :=
   178	  let bundled : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left
   179	  haveI : IsProper bundled.hom := instIsProperSndLeft C K
   180	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 bundled.hom := instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft C K
   181	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible bundled.hom := instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft C K
   182	  moduleFinite_hModule_one bundled
   183	
   184	/-! ## Item 6: acceptance smoke test
   185	
   186	The landed degree homomorphism `classDeg K` typechecks on the base-changed curve `C_K` with
   187	**every** hypothesis discharged by typeclass resolution from the instances above — no manual
   188	`haveI`/`letI`. This is the brick's acceptance criterion; the `degAt` (G-D6) spec-writer
   189	consumes exactly this. -/
   190	
   191	/-- **Item 6 (smoke test).** `classDeg K` applies to `C_K = (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` with all
   192	six instance hypotheses of the degree stack inferred automatically. -/
   193	private noncomputable def classDegBaseChangeSmoke :
   194	    Additive ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) →+ ℤ :=
   195	  classDeg K
   196	
   197	end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	/-!
    12	# Rank-one certificates for the displayed arbitrary-affine datum
    13	
    14	This file removes the caller-chosen descent stage from the certificate producer.  Starting with
    15	the displayed cocycle datum, it descends that datum to a finite stage, refines the stage until
    16	the actual pair `H^1` vanishes, runs the Noetherian rigid engine only there, and transports finite
    17	projective `H^0` back to the original coefficient ring.  Stalk rank is then computed on the
    18	original datum, so the degree law is never required away from the displayed family.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	set_option autoImplicit false
    22	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    23	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    28	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    29	open scoped TensorProduct
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    34	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    35	
    36	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    37	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    38	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    39	
    40	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    41	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    42	
    43	/-! ## Geometric inputs on the displayed datum -/
    44	
    45	/-- Residue-field divisor witnesses for the displayed cocycle datum. -/
    46	abbrev BasicOpenCocycleDatum.ResidueH1Witness
    47	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) : Prop :=
    48	  ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
    49	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing p.asIdeal.ResidueField
    50	
    51	/-- The fibrewise degree law for the class of the displayed cocycle datum. -/
    52	abbrev BasicOpenCocycleDatum.FibreClassDegree
    53	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
    54	  ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra B L]
    55	    [IsScalarTower k B L],
    56	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B L) D.cechPicClass) = (n : ℤ)
    57	
    58	namespace RankOneFamilyCertificates
    59	
    60	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
    61	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
    62	/-- Produce all four certificates for the displayed datum over an arbitrary coefficient ring.
    63	
    64	The only H1 input is a divisor witness on each residue field.  It first gives pair-H1
    65	vanishing for the displayed datum.  A finite presentation of that datum is then refined until
    66	the same pair-H1 vanishing holds at the stage itself; the Noetherian rigid engine is used only
    67	at that stage.  Its finite-projective H0 is transported back canonically, and rank one is
    68	computed on the displayed datum from its own class-degree law. -/
    69	noncomputable def ofActualDatum
    70	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    71	    (hpi : pi ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
    72	    (hW : D.ResidueH1Witness)
    73	    (hdegree : D.FibreClassDegree (genus C)) :
    74	    RankOneFamilyCertificates D := by
    75	  have hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
    76	      Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    77	    intro p
    78	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_subsingleton p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mp (hW p)
    79	  have hpair : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 :=
    80	    D.datum_subsingleton_pairH1 hpi hfib
    81	  have h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1) :=
    82	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mp hpair
    83	
    84	  obtain ⟨B0, hB0fg, D0, hD0⟩ := D.exists_fg_subalgebra_baseChange_eq
    85	  have hpairBase : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange (B' := B))).H1 := by
    86	    rw [hD0]
    87	    exact hpair
    88	  have htensor : Subsingleton ((datumPair D0).H1 ⊗[B0] B) :=
    89	    D0.subsingleton_h1_tensor_of_baseChange B hpairBase
    90	  obtain ⟨A, _, _, hAnoeth, hpairA, hAA⟩ :=
    91	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_fg_pairH1_vanishing_stage
    92	      (C := C) (pi := pi) B0 hB0fg D0 hpi htensor
    93	
    94	  letI : IsNoetherianRing A := hAnoeth
    95	  letI : Subsingleton (datumPair (D0.baseChange A)).H1 := hpairA
    96	  have hfibA : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A,
    97	      Subsingleton
    98	        ((datumPair (D0.baseChange A)).H1 ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
    99	    intro p
   100	    infer_instance
   101	  obtain ⟨_, hfiniteA, hprojectiveA⟩ :=
   102	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.datumRigidEngine (D0.baseChange A) hpi hfibA
   103	
   104	  have hbase : (D0.baseChange A).baseChange B = D := hAA.trans hD0
   105	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule (D0.baseChange A).sheaf 0
   106	  letI : Module.Finite A Q := hfiniteA
   107	  letI : Module.Projective A Q := hprojectiveA
   108	  let e : B ⊗[A] Q ≃ₗ[B] Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 :=
   109	    ((D0.baseChange A).datumH0BaseChange B hpairA).trans
   110	      (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv
   111	        (eqToIso (congrArg
   112	          (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi => E.sheaf) hbase)) 0)
   113	  letI : Module.Finite B (B ⊗[A] Q) := by infer_instance
   114	  letI : Module.Projective B (B ⊗[A] Q) := by infer_instance
   115	  have hfinite : Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   116	    Module.Finite.equiv e
   117	  have hprojective : Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) :=
   118	    Module.Projective.of_equiv e
   119	  have hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
   120	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1 :=
   121	    D.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pairH1
   122	      (n := genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C) hpair hfinite hprojective hdegree
   123	  exact ⟨h1, hfinite, hprojective, hrank⟩
   124	
   125	end RankOneFamilyCertificates
   126	
   127	end AlgebraicGeometry

    13	`RigidEngine4Assembly`, fired on the glued sheaf of a pinned basic-open cocycle datum
    14	`D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` (worksheet §3.2) through the pair data
